name: Kaustubha Eluri
bio: Kaustubha Eluri is a Full Stack Web and Mobile Developer with a strong background in AI/ML and product-driven research. He is the Developer for YouDescribeX, an AI-powered accessibility platform led by Professor Ilmi Yoon. At YouDescribeX, Kaustubha works across mobile, web, and AI systems, building cross-platform tools that generate audio descriptions for visually impaired users. His work integrates large language models, computer vision modules, and conversational features to enhance video accessibility and create inclusive digital experiences. Kaustubha’s broader research focuses on Agentic AI—intelligent systems capable of memory, reasoning, and goal-driven behavior. He is particularly interested in human-AI collaboration, mobile intelligence, and the use of generative models to address real-world challenges in accessibility, education, and responsible AI adoption.

name: Vishal Sharma
bio:
As a skilled engineer, I specialize in optimizing GPU pipeline modules through algorithm optimization and parallelization techniques. My expertise in this area allows me to identify and eliminate bottlenecks that impede performance, resulting in faster and more efficient processing. 
In addition to my work on GPU pipeline modules, I am also a seasoned backend developer, having successfully migrated code from JavaScript to TypeScript. I bring a wealth of knowledge and experience to bear on backend development projects, ensuring that systems are robust, reliable, and scalable. 
Through my passion for technology and my relentless focus on achieving excellence, I am committed to delivering high-quality results that exceed expectations. Whether working independently or as part of a team, I am dedicated to using my skills and expertise to help clients and colleagues achieve their goals and succeed in their endeavors.

bio: Manali Seth is working as a data engineer for the YouDescribe project. She is a graduate student pursuing Master of Science in Computer Science at San Francisco State University. name: Alekya Bairaboina
bio: I specialize in frontend development, focusing on React hooks to create dynamic and efficient user interfaces. By employing cutting-edge techniques like lazy loading and memoization, I optimize applications for enhanced performance. My expertise not only lies in writing code but also in comprehending the intricacies of the application, allowing me to identify potential issues and improve overall scalability. I am dedicated to crafting reliable and user-friendly applications, ensuring a seamless experience for all users. Beyond web development, I extend my skills to mobile development using React Native, delivering versatile solutions across platforms. Whether working independently or collaboratively, my commitment is to create applications that are not only functional but also valuable and enjoyable for users.

name: Caelen Wang
bio: I'm a Master's Computer Science student passionate about the intersection of machine learning and game development. In my previous project I applied pose and facial estimation to develop a webcam motion tracking feature for online multiplayer games. My work with YouDescribe involves implementing and training video captioning models that capture temporal dependencies. Through my current work in visual language modeling, I'm excited for the impact of large language models on the videogame industry.

name: Beste Yuksel
bio: Beste Filiz Yuksel received her PhD in Computer Science from Tufts University, Boston, working with Robert Jacob. Her research was on the next generation of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) that detect and evaluate real-time brain signals using machine learning classification of functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to build adaptable user interfaces for the general population. Her work won a Best Paper Award at ACM CHI 2016. She has also worked with Mary Czerwinski at Microsoft Research, investigating user-virtual agent interactions for the next generation of intelligent personal assistants. Beste will continue to work on building intelligent, adaptive interfaces that respond to both user cognitive and affective state in conjunction in her new Human-Computer Interaction lab.
